items.prompt: Does replacing row records with a Python dictionary of lists prove an Arrow-level speed improvement?

options.text: Yes, because the word column guarantees any benchmark
options.why: Performance needs a real implementation and measurement.

options.text: Yes, because Python lists have exactly Arrow's typed-buffer layout
options.why: The teaching container is not the Arrow specification.

options.text: No, because columnar engines never help analytical scans
options.why: That is an unsupported universal claim in the other direction.

options.text: No; implementation and measured workload still matter
options.why: Logical representation alone is not a performance result.

items.explanation: Separate a schema/alignment lesson from a benchmark claim. Arrow's format and execution properties are not automatically inherited by arbitrary Python containers.
